events.title: WebSocket protocol standardized
events.summary: RFC 6455 defined the WebSocket Protocol in December 2011 — full-duplex communication over a single TCP connection after an HTTP upgrade handshake.
events.about: WebSockets let browsers and servers push messages both ways without polling — chat apps, live dashboards, collaborative editors, and game servers. A client sends `Upgrade: websocket`; after the handshake, framed messages flow in both directions. Libraries like Socket.IO and native `WebSocket` in browsers build on this.

narrative.whyChosen: WebSocket ended the long-polling era for real-time web applications.
narrative.whyImportant: It became the standard transport for live UIs and event-driven backends in the browser.
narrative.problemSolved: HTTP request/response was too heavy for low-latency, server-pushed updates at scale.
